extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (U.S. citizens who are current students, recent graduates, artists, and early-career professionals) and campus Fulbright Program Advisers
extracted.subtask_description: Official eligibility rules and application-route guidance for the Fulbright U.S. Student Program, describing who may apply, which award types are available, and procedural requirements (e.g., applying through an institution or home-country commission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Current U.S. Student eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply. If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should apply through their home institution and locate the Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) on their campus to support the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Citizen (not enrolled) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply as a non-enrolled applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying; candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. See the 'Getting Started' page for eligibility details and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist (creative & performing arts) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts. Arts candidates for the U.S. Student Program should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists with more experience should consider the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of creative & performing arts projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative & Performing Arts projects are classified under the Study/Research grant category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These projects are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered; applicants should consult the specific award description for country availability and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professor/Administrator (faculty) application route
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty and administrators should pursue the Fulbright Scholar Program rather than the U.S. Student Program. Campus staff who support applicants should connect with their Fulbright Program Adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. citizen applicants (for awards to the United States)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a non-U.S. citizen interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States, you will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.S. citizens should consult the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program for routes to awards in the United States; application processes are administered locally by commissions or embassies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of awards and allowable activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Program participants pursue graduate study, conduct research, or teach English abroad; awards are available across academic disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award types include Study/Research Awards and English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards, plus special fellowships and partnership awards (e.g., Fulbright-National Geographic). Grant lengths and start dates vary by award—consult the specific award description for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application administration and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs (ECA) administers the Program under policy guidelines established by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board (FFSB), in coordination with binational commissions and foundations, U.S. embassies, and cooperating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult country- and award-specific information (e.g., award descriptions and post/commission guidance) because administration, availability, and specific requirements vary by country and award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional experience expectation for U.S. Student applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Across non-enrolled and arts applicant guidance, the Program expects relatively limited professional experience in the applicant's field—typically 7 years or less—for eligibility in the U.S. Student Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with substantially more professional experience are advised to consider the Fulbright Scholar Program instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural guidance: find local supports and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are directed to locate a Fulbright Program Adviser on their campus, consult the 'Getting Started' page, use award descriptions, and attend webinars/tutorials provided by the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the program's online resources (Award Search, Application Components, Virtual Webinars, Fulbright Online Application) and contact program staff for questions; institutional FPAs can assist with application process and requirements.
